result.markdown: --- title: "[chunk.Metric]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} A named metric value associated with a retrieved chunk. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/raghilda/blob/docs-embedding-providers/src/raghilda/chunk.py#L151-L176){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python chunk.Metric(name, value) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Metrics are used to store retrieval scores and other measurements that describe how well a chunk matches a query. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The name of the metric (e.g., "similarity", "bm25_score"). [value]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The numeric value of the metric. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#c11a174c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from raghilda.chunk import Metric similarity = Metric(name="similarity", value=0.95) print(f"{similarity.name}: {similarity.value}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` similarity: 0.95 ``` ::: :::
